issues.location: rank introduction, intuitive description before the formal definition
issues.finding: Calling rank(A) the first moment at which A is formed is one stage too late relative to the stated definition: rank(A) is the least alpha with A contained in V_alpha, while A itself first appears at the successor power-set stage. In particular, rank(empty)=0 although empty is not a member of V_0.
issues.proposed_resolution: Describe rank(A) as the earliest stage whose elements suffice to form A, and retain the exact least-ordinal definition.

issues.location: converse proof of V_alpha as the sets of rank below alpha
issues.finding: After assuming x is a member of V_alpha, the source concludes that x is not a member of V_alpha. This contradicts the premise and cannot prove the displayed characterization.
issues.proposed_resolution: The induction conclusion is rank(x) in alpha. At a successor stage x is a subset of the preceding stage; at a limit stage x already belongs to an earlier stage. These cases sharpen rank(x) less than or equal to alpha to rank(x) less than alpha.

translation_treatment: The target clarifies the stage supplying the elements of A and corrects the converse proof to conclude rank(x) in alpha, with a short successor/limit explanation. The names of Regularity and Foundation are localized inside later mathematical text. Exercises remain unfilled, other displayed formulas remain intact, and frozen source bytes are unchanged.
